name: Knowledge Graph visualization
summary: VS Code graph page for independent knowledge groups, on-demand structural views, source navigation, and low/high performance display modes.
limitations: Covers the graph page's host/client interaction and selected direct services, not all graph-generation, extraction, curation or persistence internals.
Music is included only as a consumer of group selection; sound generation and Strudel playback are outside this card.
No browser session, extension launch, installed-version check, test execution or hardware performance measurement was performed.
No existing .vscode/.knowledge graph was available in the inspected workspace for a matching group key; graph-visualization is a feature-name key.

facts.text: The visualize command opens a singleton, script-enabled Webview retained while hidden. Reopening reveals it and resends data; HTML is regenerated when its translated title changes. The ready message requests performance mode and graph data.

GraphView consumes KnowledgeGraphService.getGroups() plus entity observations. Groups preserve repeated symbols across framework/module/feature views; the aggregate snapshot instead deduplicates them. AgentGraphService reads .vscode/.knowledge/agent-graph.json, not raw structural JSON, for these curated groups.

Groups sort by order then name; the sidebar shows kind and entity/relation counts. Only the selected group renders. Its key is stored in Webview state and reused if still present, otherwise the first group wins. Empty data stops layout/animations, clears geometry cache and shows the empty state.

The page embeds browser helper strings and uses D3 SVG, zoom and force simulation. It loads extension-local dist/d3.min.js under a nonce-based CSP. package.json declares D3 ^7.9.0 and VS Code ^1.80.0; these are declared ranges, not verified installed/runtime versions.

Node hover highlights neighbors; curated-node double-click opens source, while Shift-double-click requests structural neighbors. Aggregate-node double-click opens raw structure; structural-node double-click jumps to source. Relationship tooltips expose provenance, confidence and evidence; a relationship with structuralPath supports double-click drilldown.

Advanced boundary/community/file views read StructuralGraphService and use structural-analysis aggregate/impact helpers. StructuralGraphService validates structural-graph.json and throws if missing. Errors become Webview structural status plus a VS Code warning. A new structural view replaces prior __structural_ groups; normal graph-data refresh replaces that temporary view with curated groups.

Structural overview requests at most 80 aggregate nodes. Entity-neighbor drilldown is depth 1 in both directions, capped at 80 entities/120 relations; aggregate drilldown has the same caps. Aggregation excludes within-group edges and retains at most eight raw relationship samples per aggregate edge, so its drilldown is not the complete counted relationship set.

Performance defaults to low and is machine-scoped. UI selection applies immediately, disables the selector while saving, and persists globally. Only low/high are accepted; Settings changes synchronize into the page. After a failed save the host reports the error and resends the actual preference, restoring the UI.

Low mode performs static layout in short animation-frame batches, stopping after cooling, 120 ticks or 600 ms accumulated compute time; dragging directly moves the selected node without restarting physics. High mode retains interactive force layout, particles, flow and glow. Switching mode rerenders the selected group without requesting different graph data.

Layout cache stores geometry, transform and settling state, not source/evidence objects. Node IDs and edge endpoint/verb topology determine validity, so prose changes reuse layout. Defaults bound the LRU cache to eight groups and 2,000 total nodes. Hidden pages pause layout, simulation and particles; unloading stops work and clears timers.

Missing or unreadable/invalid Agent sidecar data yields an empty Agent snapshot; the graph-data path sends groups without a generation-error field. Rendering exceptions have a separate error panel. Curated source navigation is rooted in workspaceFolders[0] and external entities are not opened as files.

Extension activation injects the knowledge and structural services. Agent sidecar create/change/delete notifications refresh the tree, open graph page and CodeLens together. The music action is another group-data consumer: it sends the selected key, but the host resolves it only among curated groups, falling back to the first group before generating code for StrudelView.

graphView.test.ts asserts the low machine default, both localized choices, valid inline JavaScript, global persistence/reopening without document reload, Settings synchronization, failed-save rollback and invalid-mode rejection. These assertions were inspected, not executed.

graphPerformanceScript.test.ts executes the shipped helper string in a mocked VM and asserts bounded/yielding layout, pause/resume/failure cleanup, cache topology invalidation/LRU/pending-state retention, and low-versus-high dragging. It is not a real-browser performance measurement; tests were not run during brief generation.

KnowledgeGraphService tests assert repeated symbols remain in independent visualization groups and group-specific IDs still resolve. The tooltip helper test asserts provenance, evidence line ranges and structural-path affordance text. Both test sources were inspected without execution.
